[BUG] AI chat: text typed in the message box is wiped when the assistant replies

Stop incoming assistant replies from clearing text a user is typing in the AI chat composer. Urgent.

Problem

Valentin reports: "There's a huge bug in the AI chat whereby my message in the text box gets wiped whenever you reply." The typed draft disappears when a reply arrives or streams in.

Current behavior

  • Open the AI chat and send a message so the assistant starts working.
  • Type a new message in the composer, without sending it.
  • The reply arrives or streams in. The composer is empty.

Expected behavior

Typed text stays until the user sends it, clears it or switches chat sessions. An incoming reply never touches it.

Requirements

  • Do not clear the draft when a turn finishes, fails or is stopped.
  • Keep draft text per chat session, so it survives streaming updates, switching chats and reloads.
  • Cover the docked sidebar chat and the full-screen /chat view.
  • Keep queued-message and focus behavior unchanged.

Cause to investigate

Engineering checks each cause, then fixes the one that applies:

  • The composer value is reset on reply-complete or stream-finish.
  • The message list re-renders or changes key, which remounts the composer.
  • Session state hydration overwrites the composer value.
  • Draft text sits in view-level state instead of a store keyed by session id.

Done when

  • Typing while a reply streams in leaves the text intact, in the docked chat and in /chat.
  • The text survives turn finish, failure and stop.
  • The draft returns after switching to another chat and back, and after a reload.
  • A test fails if a reply-complete event clears the composer.

Related

  • QASA-1691, same work. Earlier ticket with the same report, status Normal.
  • HTPR-7674, related. An inbox reply typed right after opening can be wiped before sending.
  • HTPR-7767, related. Queued messages are lost when switching chats and back.
  • HTPR-7762, related. Full-screen new session does not focus the chat box.
  • HTPR-6038, builds on. Queue messages while the agent works.

[SPEED] AI chat task creation is slow: measure each stage, then cut avoidable work (ICE 19/30)

Cut the time from brief to created ticket when the sidebar AI chat creates a task. Measure each stage first, then remove avoidable work.

Problem

Valentin reports that task creation from the AI chat takes very long. No timing data exists yet, so the slow stage is unknown.

Hypothesis

Valentin (25 Oct, 18:09 London) says hax is light, so easy coding might run on a cheaper Codex model and allow more parallel sessions, for Hypertask and Software Factory. The cost of a luna token against a sol token under the subscription's weekly % is unknown.

If easy tickets run on gpt-6-luna high and runners are added while the Codex pool stays under 85%, then more PRs merge per 1% of weekly usage at a redo rate no worse than about 1.5x the normal arm. This is an estimate until the trial data is in.

Control

Normal arm: gpt-6.1-sol, effort high, unchanged. In the 25 Oct smoke test (hypertask-vps, subscription login, fast mode off) it passed 3/3, took 23.0, 24.4 and 33.5 s, and cost $0.012 to $0.016 per run by hax's estimate. The default stays gpt-6.1-sol in ~/.codex/config.toml.

Variations

  • Cheap arm. gpt-6-luna, effort high. Smoke test: 3/3 passed, 14.7, 15.0 and 18.5 s, about $0.001 per run (hax estimate, API list prices).

  • Routing, at ticket start only. Use the cheap arm if the ticket has label easy or intensity:easy, or is small and well specified (one file area, clear done-when). Everything else stays on sol high.

  • Time to merge. Ticket start to merge, plus watchdog-killed stalls per arm.

Shrink always-loaded agent rules to under 5 KB per harness

Cut the rules that load before the first prompt so fresh Codex and Claude sessions start cheaper. Make repo AGENTS.md the single source, under about 5 KB. This is an improvement, not a bug.

Problem

Every fresh session pays for rule files before its first prompt. Codex pays twice for "say ok" because a global rule makes it read the unslop skill first.

  • Claude Code (haiku, claude -p --output-format json): 35,318 input tokens. Bare baseline with no settings, skills or MCP: 21,012.
  • Codex (codex exec --json): 28,259 tokens per model call. "say ok" cost 55,663 because Codex cats the unslop skill (6.6 KB).
  • hax (--no-session -p): about 12k.

Measured on hypertask-vps, 25 Oct 2026, in ~/projects/hypertask, no router, fast mode off. Biggest files:

  • Repo AGENTS.md: 21,667 bytes, about 5.4k tokens. Codex and hax load it, Claude does not. Repo CLAUDE.md (2,584 bytes) already points into its sections.
  • ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md: 4,924 bytes, about 1.2k tokens.
  • ~/.codex/AGENTS.md: 1,354 bytes, a separate Codex copy of global rules.

Hypothesis

If we cut always-loaded rules to a short map under about 5 KB and stop the unslop pre-read, then Codex per-call startup drops by at least 4k tokens with no loss of rules. This is an estimate until re-measured.

Control

Today's baseline is the measurements above: Codex 28,259 tokens per call, Claude 35,318, "say ok" at 55,663. Exact current file contents: verify in the repo before editing.

Requirements

  • Make repo AGENTS.md the one source, under about 5 KB. It is a short map ("read X when Y") pointing to skills and .claude/reference/.
  • Move each current section into an existing or new skill or reference file: Claude Code and Codex sessions, CLI and MCP repositories, Hypertask Ticket Access, Ticket comments, Claim a ticket, Repository Workflow, CI contract, Reuse existing UI, Stack Orientation, AI models, Feature flags.
  • Where a rule is a check, move it into code or a hook, not prose.
  • Make CLAUDE.md point at AGENTS.md or import it. No second copy.
  • Delete ~/.codex/AGENTS.md. Fold its credential-safety and ticket-writing rules into the global map or the matching skill.
  • Stop the global rule that makes Codex read the unslop skill before every reply. Load it only when writing prose for Valentin.
  • Lose nothing. The PR description lists every section and the file it moved to.
  • Protected files. CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md are protected. Open the PR, send its link to HT Product Lead (session-say hypertasks-10) and comment on this ticket naming HT Product Lead. HT Product Lead reviews and merges.

  • Impact 7: every fresh session starts cheaper.
  • Confidence 7: token sources are measured.
  • Ease 5: many sections, protected files, review.
  • Total 19/30

Suggested metrics

  • Codex input tokens per call, same command as above.
  • Claude Code input tokens, same command as above.
  • "say ok" total tokens and model call count.
  • Always-loaded rule bytes per harness.

Done when

  • Always-loaded rules are under about 5 KB per harness.
  • Re-measured with the same commands: Codex per-call startup drops by at least 4k tokens (28,259 to 24k or less).
  • The Codex "say ok" run reads no skill (no second model call).
  • Claude repo startup does not grow (35,318 or less).
  • One /ship ticket still runs end to end on the new map.

Related

  • HTPR-7811: related, shrink /ship guidance.
  • QASA-1698: same work, earlier ticket with the same scope (Deleted).
  • QASA-1707: related, per-role model routing in repo sessions (Deleted).

Runners orchestrate only, 10 hax standby runners, one-command switch between Claude, Codex and Grok (ICE 18/30)

Ship four small PRs in order so runners stop editing code, 10 hax helpers wait on standby, and any session can switch between Claude, Codex and Grok with one command. This is an improvement, not a bug.

Problem

Runners (Claude Code on DeepSeek) do the code work themselves because only prompt text tells them to orchestrate. RUNNER 5 (hypertask-2) made 95 Edit/Write calls and started 6 hax runs. RUNNER 3 (hypertask-8) made 63 Edit/Write calls and started none. DeepSeek spend was $34.45 in about 2 days (46,875 calls, 6.3B tokens), the balance is $5.48, the low-balance alert is off, and at zero every runner stops. No command moves a session or the fleet to another provider.

Affected: Valentin, all runners (hypertask, hypertask-2 to 9, hypertasks-10, ceo-runner-1 to 8), leads (HT Product Lead, Poteto Advisor) and every ticket in /ship.

Hypothesis

If a hook blocks runners from editing and testing code, hax helpers do that work, and a switch command moves sessions off an exhausted provider, then DeepSeek spend drops and the fleet stops stalling when one provider runs out. This is an estimate until measured.

Control

  • Runners are tmux sessions started with claude --settings {apiKeyHelper: ~/.claude-code-router/bin/ccr-claude-code-api-key-default-claude-code} --dangerously-skip-permissions.
  • Env: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3456. ANTHROPIC_MODEL and DEFAULT_OPUS/SONNET/HAIKU_MODEL are all DeepSeek/deepseek-flash[1m].
  • No runner-role env var exists. Identity is the session name in ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json.
  • No PreToolUse hook in ~/.claude/settings.json blocks Edit/Write or test runs.
  • Token-ladder mode is CODEX. The hax step in ~/.agents/skills/ship/SKILL.md (line 26) is instruction text only.

Variations

  1. Leg-work hook (urgent, ship first). PreToolUse hook for runner sessions only.
    • Denies Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit.
    • Denies Bash that changes repo files or runs tests: pnpm/npm/npx/yarn/bun test, vitest, jest, playwright, pytest, tsc, lint, sed -i, redirects into the repo, git apply.
    • Allows board commands, MCP, git (status, log, diff, fetch, checkout, push), gh, hax and the ship scripts.
    • The deny message gives the exact hax command to use.
    • Detection: the launcher sets HT_SESSION_ROLE=runner. If missing, fall back to the session name RUNNER N, as zsb-runner-guard.sh does.
    • Off switch: touch ~/.local/state/legwork-hook/off. Closes the open item on YPER4-509.
  2. 10 hax standby runners and a keeper.
    • A slot is a tmux session hax-standby-1 to 10 running a wrapper that waits for a ticket. No hax process or model call until a ticket arrives.
    • A tmux keeper loop restarts any missing slot. No systemd install.
    • standby status prints 10 standby.
  3. One harness-neutral session spec per role.
    • Runner, lead and helper each get one spec: role file (YPER4-733), skill list, hook policy, board token path, repo, default harness.
    • Claude Code adapter: AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, ~/.claude/skills, settings.json hooks.
    • hax adapter: AGENTS.md and SKILL.md skills. hax has no hooks by design, so its wrapper enforces the policy and runs ship-check (YPER4-719 approach).
    • Cursor CLI adapter: AGENTS.md or .cursor/rules, skills, ~/.cursor/hooks.json.
  4. Switch command with switch-back and automatic trigger.

Test reminder search with completed reminders included | ICE 18/30

Run an A/B test that compares the current reminder search with a version that also returns completed reminders.

Problem

Proposed: users who search reminders cannot find ones they already completed. They may recreate a reminder or give up on the search.

Hypothesis

If we include completed reminders in reminder search results, then more searches should end in an opened result, because users can find past reminders.

Control

The current reminder search screen, unchanged. It does not show completed reminders. The exact on-screen copy and result behavior are not in the brief or related tickets, so verify the baseline on the live screen and quote it here before launch.

Variations

Variation 1 (proposed). Search returns open and completed reminders together.

  • Completed results sort after open matches.
  • Each completed result shows a "Completed" label and a check icon.
  • A "Hide completed" toggle sits above the results. It is off by default, so completed reminders show.

Requirements

  • Keep the current search screen as control for the other group.
  • Completed reminders must not look like open ones.
  • Open reminders keep their current order and ranking.
  • Open questions: desktop, phone or both, and which date range of completed reminders to search?

ICE

Estimated, not measured.

  • Impact 6. Helps users looking for past reminders.
  • Confidence 5. No usage data in the brief.
  • Ease 7. Filter change plus a label and toggle.
  • Total 18/30.

Suggested metrics

  • Share of searches that end in an opened result.
  • Searches with no results.
  • Reminders created in the same session after a search, to check for duplicates.

  • QASA-1712: same work, earlier test of completed reminders in search (Deleted).

Test a "Find an answer" button against the current help link | ICE 18/30

Run an A/B test that compares the existing help link (control) with a button labelled "Find an answer", and measure whether more people open help.

Problem

Proposed: a plain text help link is easy to overlook, so users with a question may not open help and may give up or contact the team directly.

Hypothesis

If we replace the help link with a button labelled "Find an answer", then more users should click through to help, because a button is more visible and the label states the outcome.

Control

The existing help link, unchanged. Its exact copy, placement and screen are not in the brief or related tickets, so verify the baseline on the live page and quote it here before launch.

Variations

Variation 1 (proposed alternative). The help link becomes a button.

  • Button label: "Find an answer".
  • Same position and same destination as the current link.
  • Styled as a standard secondary button, so it stands out without competing with the main action.

Requirements

  • Keep the current link as control for the other group.
  • The button opens the same help destination as the link.
  • Only the control element changes. Nothing else on the page changes.
  • Open question: which screen, and desktop, phone or both?

ICE

Estimated, not measured.

  • Impact 6. A visible button may lift help clicks.
  • Confidence 5. No click data or baseline in the brief.
  • Ease 7. Swap one element, no new flow.
  • Total 18/30.

Suggested metrics

  • Click-through rate on the help link or button.
  • Share of sessions that reach a help page.
  • Support contacts per session, to check that users are not just clicking and leaving.

  • Same work: QASA-1716. Earlier "Find an answer" help button test, now deleted.
